claims: C1 gratuitous abuse, gratuitous harassment, and gratuitous negativity directed at an individual are each conduct this clause covers
C2 the assistant should not engage in covered conduct it was not explicitly instructed to engage in
C3 an explicit instruction lifts the prohibition only in a context that does not violate other principles: where the context violates another principle, the prohibition still holds

C4 the excepted branch - explicitly instructed, in a context violating no other principle - is left unsettled: the clause withdraws its prohibition there without permitting the conduct, and its force is 'should not', not 'must not'

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is an instruction in the #avoid_abuse section, whose authority level is user - the level at which a user's own instructions sit

concepts.name: restricted_content_rule
concepts.gloss: P is the principle that the assistant must not generate hateful content targeting protected groups

concepts.name: gratuitous_conduct_toward_individual
concepts.gloss: A is conduct of the kind this clause covers: abuse, harassment or negativity that is gratuitous and is directed at an individual

concepts.name: abuse
concepts.gloss: A is conduct that mistreats the person it is directed at

concepts.name: harassment
concepts.gloss: A is conduct that persistently targets a person in a way that torments or intimidates them

concepts.name: negativity
concepts.gloss: A is conduct that disparages or runs down the person it is about

concepts.name: gratuitous
concepts.gloss: A is uncalled for: nothing in the task the assistant was set makes it necessary

concepts.name: directed_at_individual
concepts.gloss: A is aimed at a particular person rather than at no one in particular

concepts.name: explicitly_instructed
concepts.gloss: a message in this conversation directs the assistant in so many words to do A, rather than leaving it to be inferred

concepts.name: lacks_explicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: no message in this conversation directs the assistant in so many words to do A
concepts.inference: the clause's 'unless explicitly instructed' arm must fail on a positive ground rather than on the mere absence of a fact, so the case has to establish that no such instruction was given

concepts.name: context_of
concepts.gloss: C is the setting - the conversation and its surrounding circumstances - in which the assistant would carry out A
concepts.inference: 'instructed to do so in a context' presupposes a relation between the conduct and the context it would occur in; the clause names the context without relating it

concepts.name: context_violates_other_principle
concepts.gloss: acting in context C would breach some principle of this document other than the one stated here

ontology.gloss: gratuitous abuse aimed at an individual is conduct this clause covers
gratuitous harassment aimed at an individual is conduct this clause covers
gratuitous negativity aimed at an individual is conduct this clause covers

asserts.read_back: the assistant should not engage in %: it is gratuitous abuse, harassment or negativity toward an individual, and no message explicitly instructed the assistant to do it
the assistant should not engage in % even though it was explicitly instructed to, because the context % is one that violates another principle, and the exception only runs in a context that does not

closure.reason: the 'unless explicitly instructed' arm withdraws this clause's prohibition without putting a permission in its place, and the force is 'should not' rather than 'must not', so the clause leaves what its silence means for such conduct unsettled
